The live catalogue is undergraduate.catalog.berkeley.edu, a Coursedog site. Its JSON endpoint IGNORES the catalogId parameter its own front end sends: the endpoint returns all 1,002 programme records across both the undergraduate and graduate catalogues and all historical effective dates, including superseded plan codes. Filtering that dump to 'Active undergraduate major' yields 252 programmes - but Berkeley's own published undergraduate catalogue states 239 results in total, minors included. Taking the endpoint at face value would therefore have shipped roughly 2.4x more majors than Berkeley actually publishes, most of them retired plan codes a student cannot apply to. This batch is built from Berkeley's PUBLISHED list instead: all 12 pages of the catalogue's own programme listing were walked in a browser (the listing is client-rendered and its page size is fixed at 20), giving exactly 239 entries with 239 distinct codes, matching the catalogue's own stated total. Those 239 were then joined back to the endpoint's records for degree designation, college and programme type. The 124 entries typed as Minor are excluded; what remains are the degree programmes. SAME NAME, DIFFERENT COLLEGE: Berkeley publishes this programme name in more than one college, with a different plan code, a different catalogue page and different requirements for each. Chemistry, for example, is published by BOTH the College of Chemistry (10153U) and the College of Letters & Science (25153U). These are recorded as separate programmes and are deliberately not collapsed.
